title: What will Fed Rate hit before 2027?
description:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the lower or the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal fund range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if the lower or the upper bound of the target federal funds rate reaches the specified level at any point by December 31, 2026, 12:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No.”

Emergency rate cuts and hikes outside the regularly scheduled meetings will be considered.

The resolution source for this market is the official website of the Federal Reserve at:
https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.

This market may resolve as soon as the relevant data showing the reached level is published.

eventMetadata.context_description: The federal funds rate target range stands at 3.50%–3.75% following the July 29 FOMC decision, unchanged for the fifth straight meeting amid 3.4% July CPI and resilient economic activity. Three dissents favoring a 25-basis-point hike highlight internal division, while futures markets price the effective rate near 3.8% by November 2026 and about 4% by mid-2027. Trader positioning on the Polymarket reflects consensus that the lower bound will reach 3.5% before 2027, with only modest probability assigned to the upper bound hitting 4.25% or higher, driven by persistent inflation pressures relative to the 2% goal and limited scope for easing. The September 15–16 FOMC meeting, with updated projections, and subsequent labor-market and inflation releases will shape near-term path expectations.
